analysis.title: GS Basics - Resilient. Inflation Persistent. Home Drones
key_insights: CPI printed hot across the board: headline +0.4%, core +0.3%, with strength beyond energy in medical services, insurance and other categories. The author says it is hard to dismiss as energy pass-through and that underlying inflation is sticky.
With the hot CPI and hawkish comments from Waller and Logan, markets are pricing a December hike plus some optionality of 50bp, and further tightening into 2027. The curve is bear flattening.
SPX barely fell on the CPI day and futures were recovering the next morning. AI sentiment appears to be improving, supporting the core engines of the market.
VIX briefly traded into the 20s but finished below 20. The author reads this as positioning doing more to support the tape than macro is doing to undermine it.
Neocloud commentary overnight was broadly supportive. Data center capacity constraints remain the primary operational bottleneck and compute utilization across major providers is elevated.
Market focus in AI is concentrated on hardware delivery and developer coding workflows. Broader edge and enterprise autonomous integrations are at earlier stages of deployment.

Rubio, after the G7 meetings in Paris, signaled the administration favors sustained economic pressure and the naval blockade over an immediate return to major combat operations. Per wire reports, Qatari mediators are working within an estimated two week diplomatic window, with official parameters unconfirmed.

Brent has bounced off yesterday's lows but directional conviction is low. If Brent consolidates near $90 with collapsing realized volatility, equities should increasingly look through the headline noise.
Rates are a headwind but the market has built a cushion from the prior rally. Yields need another leg higher before they become a material problem for equities, since the rate of change matters.
Credit is the one to watch, with high yield spreads chopping sideways. Cyclicality relative to the market is holding in.

There is a reflexivity with energy: higher oil, stickier inflation, a more hawkish Fed. The open question is whether the Fed is reacting to energy effects already past or to something more persistent.

Gross exposure has been cut, nets are historically low and appetite to add risk has diminished substantially. The author calls this a tailwind for the tape, and says elevated volatility relative to price action should decay absent fresh negative news.
Veterans Day: the bond market is closed and equities are open. The author is watching the neoclouds and the next move in energy.

tension_points.bear_case: Underlying inflation is sticky beyond energy, markets price a December hike with 50bp optionality and more tightening into 2027, and yields could take another leg higher.
